discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France; Flatiron Institute; University of Geneva

subfield: Theoretical condensed matter physics (strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that lattice fermion models become exactly solvable in infinite dimensions, and Georges and Kotliar mapped the lattice problem onto a self-consistent quantum impurity model. That mapping is dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It gave the first non-perturbative, controlled description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It explained how quasiparticles and Hubbard bands coexist in correlated metals, and its predictions have been confirmed repeatedly by photoemission and optics. Combined with density functional theory, DMFT became the standard quantitative framework for real correlated materials: transition-metal oxides, actinides, iron pnictides, nickelates and cuprates. Its cluster and non-equilibrium extensions now drive progress on the many-electron problem worldwide. DMFT changed how physicists understand and compute electronic correlation. It has the depth, rigour and lasting impact the Prize recognizes.
